text:
alex: Heads-up: hitting an allocator handoff race in paged-attn KV pager during high QPS (flashvariant run). Seeing repeated alloc failures and transient OOMs when bursty batching is enabled.

maria: Which benchmark/test? any repro steps? stack traces?

alex: Repro is easy-ish on local. run: `bench_kv_pager --workload=flash-burst --gpus=1 --concurrency=48`
Logs show handoff path failing to reserve slab after the producer believes it handed ownership. snippet:
```
E 2026-03-17T18:03:21.123Z kv_pager: reserve_slab failed err=ENOMEM slab_id=0x7f9a3c
W 2026-03-17T18:03:21.124Z handoff: commit failed preempted_by=reclaim slab_id=0x7f9a3c
I 2026-03-17T18:03:21.125Z slab_reclaim: reclaiming slab_id=0x7f9a3c owner=none
```
Observed pattern: handoff flips owner->none, concurrent reclaim observes none and reclaims before handoff finalizes. result = failed reserve + client-facing tail latency spike.

priya: That looks like a classic window-of-no-ownership race. Are we relying on a two-step non-atomic state flip?

alex: yeah, code does `slab.owner = none; notify(handoff_q);` then producer continues and expects to set owner=producer after getting ack. If reclaim runs between those lines, we get double-free.

david: I traced a run and put a trace link: /traces/3187654321 (contains handoff timeline). The reclaim path runs ~250us after owner->none in the failing runs.

maria: Two quick options: make the handoff an atomic CAS on a tagged owner field (owner + epoch) or move reclaim to happen only after handoff ACK (but that increases memory hold time). Which is cheaper?

priya: I'd prefer CAS+epoch. Add a short-lived handoff epoch that the producer writes and the reclaim checks. Minimal pause. Also add backoff on reserve path.

alex: Trying a minimal patch locally: use `compare_exchange_strong(&slab.owner_tag, expected_tag, new_tag)` and set expected_tag to (none, epoch) -> new_tag (producer, epoch+1)\npatch:
```c
// sketch
uint64_t old_tag = slab.owner_tag.load();
if (old_tag == TAG_NONE) {
  uint64_t new_tag = make_tag(PRODUCER, old_tag.epoch+1);
  if (slab.owner_tag.compare_exchange_strong(old_tag, new_tag)) {
    // got it, continue handshake
  } else {
    // retry path
  }
}
```

maria: Also add telemetry counters: `handoff_retries`, `slab_reclaimed_during_handoff`, `alloc_fail_during_handoff`. We can then evaluate frequency under corporate burst traces.

david: Agreed. And add a debug log that prints both owner_tag and reclaim_epoch when reclaim happens.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for branch=handshake-fix, env=perf-canary.

alex: Quick canary run results (small): 10k requests flash-burst, before: 1.9% alloc-fail, p99 latency 310ms. after CAS-epoch patch + small backoff: alloc-fail 0.03%, p99 254ms. Alloc-fail spikes gone in this run.

priya: nice! can we run a longer stress (1h) with concurrency ramp to validate abort cases?

alex: yes running 1h now on perf-canary-2. Will post full numbers.

maria: If the long-run looks stable, we'll include patch + telemetry, then cut a tiny revert-safe rollout (canary -> 20% -> 100%). Also document the design in the pager README.

alex: FYI patch is on PR #4521 (handshake-fix). I'll add the logs + counters requested.

david: Also note: spotted some smaller latencies due to reduced retry thrash (was spinning trying to reserve). So aside from correctness, this helps perf.

alex: final note: we should also audit other handoff paths in paged-attn (slotmap, pagehouse) — pattern may repeat.

maria: +1. create follow-up issue to sweep similar handoff code.

alex: Will do. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
